- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates sharp drops; add buffer for downside risk or adjust downward early.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–10 days) after spikes; apply lag correction or dampen initial slope.
- After a price spike (e.g., >78), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +2–3% above peak or use mean-reversion anchor.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; introduce sentiment-triggered mean-reversion or downward bias adjustment.
- Model ignores sentiment-driven volatility in the last 3–5 days; weight recent sentiment more heavily in final 10–15 days of forecast.
